original_content.knowledge_point: Constructing a Sum of Line Integrals With Respect to X, Y, and Z
original_content.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}2y\,dx+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dy+3z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=\,i+t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [1,3]?$
original_content.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=1,\,y(t)=t,\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}2y\,dx+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dy+3z\,dz & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+3z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(2y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+3z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2t\cdot (0)+\operatorname{ln}⁡1\cdot (1)+3{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}6{t}^{2}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.knowledge_point: Constructing a Sum of Line Integrals With Respect to X, Y, and Z
corrected_content.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}2y\,dx+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dy+3z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=\,i+t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [1,3]?$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Along $C$, $x(t)=1$, $y(t)=t$, and $z(t)=t^2$, so $x'(t)=0$, $y'(t)=1$, and $z'(t)=2t$. Substitute both the coordinates and their derivatives:

$$\int_C 2y\,dx+\ln x\,dy+3z\,dz
=\int_1^3\left(2t\cdot0+\ln(1)\cdot1+3t^2\cdot2t\right)\,dt
=\int_1^3 6t^3\,dt.$$

Thus the equivalent integral is $\int_1^3 6t^3\,dt$, and its value is $[\tfrac32t^4]_1^3=120$.

The original source accepted $\int_1^3 6t^2\,dt$ and its worked solution changed $3t^2\cdot2t$ into $6t^2$. That simplification loses a factor of $t$. The study choice replaces that exponent with $3$; all other original choices are retained.
